chunks: They brought [to their father Jacob] upon his shirt with false blood. He said: "No, your souls have enticed you to something. So patience is most fitting. And Allah is the one sought for help against what you describe."

key_terms.أَنفُسُكُمْ: your souls (the internal source of the deception)
key_terms.الْمُسْتَعَانُ: the one sought for help (Allah as the source of aid)
key_terms.بِدَمٍ كَذِبٍ: with false blood (the deceptive evidence sent by the brothers)
key_terms.سَوَّلَتْ: enticed/allured (referring to the soul's role in suggesting evil)
key_terms.صَبْرٌ جَمِيلٌ: beautiful patience (a specific type of patient endurance without complaint)
key_terms.قَمِيصٍ: shirt (a key object in the narrative of Joseph)

ai.seo_question: What is the meaning of 'sabr jamil' in the story of Prophet Jacob?
ai.summary: In Shia exegesis, this verse highlights Prophet Jacob’s (AS) intuitive discernment (kashf) against superficial evidence, as he recognizes the blood as fabricated despite its physical presence. His declaration of 'beautiful patience' (sabr jamil) is viewed not merely as passive endurance but as an active, dignified spiritual state that anticipates divine resolution, serving as a model for believers facing familial betrayal. The phrase 'what you describe' (ma tasifun) underscores the contrast between the brothers' external narrative and the internal reality of their souls' deceit.
